purpose: Additional statement and source-metadata retrieval for Word Cloud and Walrus Weights. Evidence provenance and long-scenario qualification remain separate.

records.title: Word Cloud

sources.observation: The page contains the full Word Cloud problem statement, input/output, constraints, typography formulas, and three sample data sets. It explicitly links to the Kattis wordcloud problem.
Maps Word Cloud / wordcloud to mcpc-2014.
The Kattis problem entry exposes source metadata naming ACM/ICPC Mid-Central USA 2014 Regional Contest and authors Ryan Marshall and Michael Goldwasser.

observedContent.scenario: A data collector creates word clouds from word-frequency counts; each word receives a point size, fixed-width font dimensions are calculated, and words are packed in their given order into rows under a maximum cloud width.
observedContent.mechanics: Font size formula, character-width ceiling calculation, horizontal spacing, greedy row packing, row height as maximum word font size, total cloud height as sum of row heights.
observedContent.inputOutput: Multiple data sets with W and N, followed by word/count pairs; output a numbered CLOUD height per data set.

records.rationale: The statement has a concrete data-processing narrative and several interacting layout calculations, and is materially richer than a one-formula exercise. However, the core task remains a single ordered greedy row-packing process; the submitted STRONG classification is not yet justified. Provisional MODERATE only, pending original contest-host statement retrieval and human rubric confirmation.

records.title: Walrus Weights

sources.observation: The Kattis problem entry identifies Walrus Weights / walrusweights, source Popup 2015 Session 1, and author Marc Vinyals.
No Walrus Weights row was found in the consulted ICPC archive index; this is consistent with Popup being outside that archive's indexed contest set and is not evidence against the source.

records.rationale: This improves source provenance beyond the earlier generic VJudge listing, but no complete statement, constraints, or scenario evidence has been captured. Keep the human-review flag and do not infer long-scenario eligibility from the title or known algorithm pattern.
